title: The Top of the Eiffel Tower Draws a Small Circle Each Day to Dodge the Sun
hook: On a clear day, the top of the Eiffel Tower moves in a circle about 15 cm across

open.title: The Eiffel Tower leans a little every sunny day, and the wind has nothing to do with it
open.line: A 330 meter iron tower moves a little on clear days. It isn't the wind. So what is pushing it?

summary: Only the side of the Eiffel Tower facing the sun expands, so the top leans away from the sun. On a clear day the top traces a circle about 15 cm across.

text: On a clear day, the top of the Eiffel Tower doesn't stay still.
The Eiffel Tower's ironwork weighs 7300 tons.

panels.text: So it grows taller in the heat?

text: According to the official explanation, it does get taller.
The bigger movement actually happens sideways.
The sun hits only one of the tower's four sides at a time.
Only the sunny side expands, so the top leans away from the sun.
As the sun crosses the sky, the top moves around with it.
On a clear day it traces a circle about 15 cm across.
There is even a record that in the 1976 heat wave, the sway at the top reached 18 cm.
